title: Fastpath: Thermal Trip Recovery — On-call Notes & Runbook Sketch
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a fast, pragmatic sketch for first responders when a rack or node triggers a thermal trip (GPU temps spike -> emergency throttle/shutdown -> degraded capacity). Focus is on getting serving back quickly with minimal correctness impact; long-term root-cause and postmortem belong in a follow-up. Covers: detection, safe isolation, temporary capacity add, GPU replacement cadence, quick comms, and critical observability checks.

When to use this vs full runbook
- Use this when telemetry shows: multiple PGPU_FATAL/thermal events in a short window, or a single node triggers emergency_shutdown and queued requests backlog grows > 2x baseline.
- If there's a datacenter power issue or building HVAC alarm, escalate to facilities; this doc assumes node-level thermal trips (fans, VRMs, thermal sensors).

Preflight checks (5m)
- Check Grafana: node GPU temp chart, fan rpm, power draw, GPU_util, and node-level CPU temp. Confirm pattern: temp rising then abrupt GPU down/0% util.
- Check k8s node status: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep <node>
- Check device-level logs: ssh root@<node> and inspect dmesg, /var/log/messages, nvidia-smi pmon, and vendor telemetry.
- Verify no simultaneous infra events (BMC flapping, OOB network down).
- If multiple racks affected, contact oncall infra lead immediately.

Fast recovery plan (steps to run in order)
1) Detect & Triage (0–5m)
- Alert from monitor: "gpu-thermal-trip" triggered -> open incident channel #sre-hotfix.
- Identify scope (single GPU, host, rack). Use query: metric{event="thermal_trip"} by (node).
- Quick health call (voice) if >1 rack impacted: senior-sre, infra oncall, hw-ops.

2) Protect traffic (5–10m)
- Immediately mark problematic node as unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node>.
- Drain live pods with conservative grace to preserve KV cache for model inference: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=45 --timeout=10m.
- If draining causes cascading failures in autoscaler, set cluster-autoscaler to no-scale temporarily.

3) Short-term capacity injection (5–20m)
- If Dedicated pool has warm spare nodes, attach warm spare to pool (console) and mark capacity as available.
- If no spare, perform emergency spot spinup in same AZ with matching accelerator profile (follow capacity playbook for fastpath images).
- Tip: use the pre-baked A/B image tag: infra:fastpath-2025-02. This image has no heavy initialization of model cache.

4) Quick hardware triage & safe reset (10–30m)
- SSH to node, run: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200; sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 200; nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=name,used_memory --format=csv
- If logs show thermal sensor asserts or VRM errors, do not immediately reseat GPU. Prefer controlled reboot first.
- Soft reboot sequence: sudo systemctl stop containerd && sudo reboot --force. Watch BMC for host hang.
- If host fails to POST or BMC shows fan failure, tag node for replacement (see "Replace GPU / node" below).

5) Replace GPU vs. Replace Node (decision flow)
- If only GPU device shows errors (and other hardware OK), schedule GPU cartridge replacement (HW ops).
- If BMC, NIC, or motherboard logs are noisy, escalate to full node replacement.
- For GPU replace: follow physical-swap checklist (ESD safe, cold-swap if supported). If cold-swap required, schedule brief maintenance window and drain all pods first.

6) Post-recover validation (after reinsertion / reboot)
- Run smoke tests: sample inference calls for 3 popular models (short prompts) hitting the node directly if possible. Validations: latency < SLO, correct logits shape, no CUDA errors in logs.
- Validate KV cache behavior: for models with large KV caches, confirm cache warmup doesn't overload the node. If it does, throttle batch size at edge while cache warms.
- Mark node schedulable only after passing smoke tests and 15m stable metrics. kubectl uncordon <node>.

Observability & quick commands (cheat sheet)
- Grafana boards: SRE -> GPU -> temps-by-rack; Alerts: gpu-temp-trip, gpu-fan-fail, bmc-flap.
- Useful commands:
  - kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
  - kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=45
  - ssh hwops@<bmc> (use jump for OOB)
  - nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE,POWER,FAN,PCI -i 0
  - sudo ethtool -S <nic> (look for link flaps)
  - journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -i therm

Customer & internal comms (templates)
- Internal incident slack snippet (post to #sre-hotfix):
  "Short: thermal trip on node <node> in <az>. Cordoned + draining. Injecting spare capacity (or spinning up spot). ETA for recovery ~30–60m. Impact: degraded capacity for <model-team> — rate-limit applied. Lead: @AishaK. More details: <incident-doc-link>."

- Customer short update (for CS/GTM if customer impacted):
  "We observed a thermal-related hardware event affecting a subset of inference capacity in <region>. Our engineers isolated the impacted host(s), injected spare capacity to maintain steady throughput, and are replacing the affected hardware. There is no data exposure. We'll share a follow-up with root cause and mitigation steps."

Quick heuristics and hacks (things that saved time in past incidents)
- If cache warmup is killing newly added nodes, temporarily mute model warmup hooks and allow traffic to flow slowly (reduce batch size and concurrency limiter).
- NVLink/rail errors often show as repeated PCIe errors in dmesg — if you see repeated pcie AER errors, prefer node replacement instead of just GPU swap.
- For thermal trips during heavy retraining or evals (batch jobs), preferentially bump those jobs to preemptible capacity before forcing customer-facing pods into drains. Communicate to Research.

Post-incident checklist (owners and timelines)
- Within 12h: hw-ops to submit repair ticket with part serials and photo logs. (owner: hw-ops)
- Within 24h: SRE to collect debug bundle and attach to JIRA-SRE-4821 (owner: Aisha). Include: dmesg, journalctl, nvidia-smi output, BMC logs, rack power telemetry.
- 48–72h: complete RCA draft and mitigation plan (thermals -> replace airflow baffles? change fan curves? upgrade firmware?) (owner: infra-lead).

Notes / open questions (to tidy in final runbook)
- Need a clear policy for cold-swap vs hot-swap for our current GPU chassis (ask hw-ops for explicit step-by-step).
- Consider adding automatic temporary-weight-zero policy in router for nodes that are cordoned due to thermal alarms.

Raw log examples (placeholders)
- dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (13) — GPU has fallen off the bus"
- journalctl: "nvidia-persistenced: Thermal shutdown requested by driver"

Appendix: commands to collect debug bundle (single script suggestion)
- sudo mkdir -p /tmp/sre-debug && sudo cp /var/log/messages /tmp/sre-debug/messages.log || true
- sudo dmesg > /tmp/sre-debug/dmesg.log
- nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/sre-debug/nvidia-smi.xml || nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/sre-debug/nvidia-smi.txt
- tar czf /tmp/sre-debug-<node>-$(date +%F).tgz /tmp/sre-debug && upload to s3://redwood-debug-bundles/<node>/

TODOs (follow-up work)
- Formalize thermal sensor thresholds and alert routing (owner: observability).
- Decide on fan-curve tuning experiments with hw vendor (owner: infra-research).

Endnotes
- This is intentionally terse and messy — intended for oncall quick use. Convert to canonical runbook after 1–2 incidents and include vendor replacement SOPs and part numbers.
